claims.statement: The revised EUDR applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and for micro or small operators already covered by the prior timber regime; most other micro and small operators receive until 30 June 2027.
Even after the 2025 simplification, operators must retain supply-chain records, while competent authorities can check due-diligence systems and records and conduct audits and apply penalties.

Hypothesis: a corridor-specific supplier portal can outperform broad enterprise tools for Polish importers because it can localize evidence requests, normalize recurring supplier defects, and distribute through customs brokers.

contrary_evidence: The regulation has already been postponed and simplified, reducing urgency and the data burden for some SME roles.
Large traceability vendors, certification schemes, and ERP providers are already targeting EUDR compliance.

economics.acquisition_route: Win one customs broker or ERP implementer serving a narrow timber corridor and share compliant supplier onboarding materials
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 120 importers at 60k PLN blended ARR yield 7.2M PLN ARR and about 2.2M PLN EBITDA by year 6. At 3.5x EBITDA and 65% ownership, equity is about 5M PLN in years 6 to 8; concentration in one regulatory deadline is the largest fragility.
economics.founder_time: 15 to 20 hours weekly for the first corridor, then 10 to 15 hours with supplier-support contractors
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70% to 82% after supplier support and expert exception review; automated retention and exports are high margin
economics.payback: A buyer can justify annual fees if the rail protects shipment continuity and removes repeated supplier chasing; quantify current labor and delay first
economics.pricing: 25,000 to 60,000 PLN onboarding plus 2,000 to 6,000 PLN monthly and 50 to 200 PLN per shipment
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every shipment, supplier, harvest plot, risk update, and five-year evidence-retention obligation creates repeat use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A corridor-specific supplier evidence and exception graph showing recurring missing fields, risk signals, and accepted remediation
fingerprint.customer: Mid-sized Polish furniture and wood-component manufacturers acting as EUDR operators for non-EU timber inputs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Customs brokers, timber-certification auditors, sector ERP implementers, and furniture-export associations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Localized supplier portal, lot-to-plot evidence graph, exception review, and DDS-ready export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer pays at corridor onboarding, per shipment, and annually for supplier and evidence retention
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A purchase order or shipment needs plot, legality, risk, and due-diligence evidence before customs or EU market placement

founder_fit: The founder's data engineering and Polish/EU context fit a rules-and-provenance product, while broker and ERP channels reduce direct social selling. It is part-time feasible after narrowing to one corridor, though independent forestry and legal expertise is essential.
risks: Supplier evidence can be false, incomplete, or impossible to verify remotely.
Sanctions, conflict, privacy, and geolocation sensitivity vary by sourcing corridor.
Further legislative delays or a low-risk country classification can reduce near-term demand.

structure.control_point: The immutable lot-to-plot evidence packet attached before shipment market placement
structure.critical_dependency: Upstream suppliers must provide verifiable geolocation and legality evidence early enough to keep shipments moving

thesis: Build a supplier-facing evidence rail for mid-sized Polish furniture and wood-component manufacturers that first place non-EU timber products on the EU market. It would collect plot geolocation and legality evidence, bind supplier declarations to lots and shipments, run risk and completeness checks, preserve five-year provenance, and export a due-diligence-statement-ready packet plus downstream references. Start with one narrow origin-and-product corridor and a customs-broker channel, not an all-commodity ESG platform.
title: EUDR Plot-to-Shipment Rail for Polish Furniture Importers
uncertainties: Exact product codes, operator role, and deadline for each target furniture or component importer.
Supplier willingness and ability to provide reliable plot polygons and legal-harvest evidence.
Whether a single corridor has enough annual shipments and paying importers for a beachhead.
